name: Del Moreau
equipment: A black velvet evening coat with a fake ermine collar (no armor)
Derringer (Remington over-and-under), 2 rounds loaded, in her evening bag
Evening clothes: two gowns, one good, one that looks good under lights
Makeup case with a mirror, a false bottom, and a set of lock picks she is not supposed to have
Sheet music stamped THE SEA LION CLUB, COLUMBUS AVE.
Matchbooks from eleven different clubs, for credibility
Three sets of calling cards for three women who do not exist
features: Knows the Block (City-Born origin, San Francisco: she knows which alleys go through, which bars belong to whom, and has advantage on Streetwise checks to find a person, place or service in the city)

The Long Con (she keeps up to 2 prepared cover identities; advantage on Deception, Performance and Persuasion to keep one up; casual checks against it pass without a roll. Current covers: Mrs. Adele Varney, a widow from Pasadena with money; Miss Dottie Fair, a cigarette girl looking for work)
Cheap Shot (once per turn, +2d6 damage with a finesse melee weapon or a sidearm when she has advantage, an ally is next to the target, or the target believed a lie she told it in the last minute)
Quick Hands (bonus action: Dash, Disengage, Hide, or a Sleight of Hand check)
Racket: Roper (anyone she has talked to for 10 minutes treats her as a friend until given a reason not to, and will do a favor that costs them nothing without a check)
Back Door of Every Club (Nightclub Singer background: she can get in the stage door of any club in the city and knows the bartender's name)

personality.traits: I flirt with everybody, men, women, dogs and lieutenants, because it is easier than meaning it. I sing under my breath when I am lying. I always know where the exits are.
personality.ideals: Everybody is running a con. The only sin is running one on somebody who cannot afford to lose.
personality.bonds: Ned Corrigan got me out of the Women's Jail in 1931 and gave me a job instead of a lecture. I have roped for the agency ever since. I owe Cass Delaney for something she has never mentioned, and I owe Ned for everything.
personality.flaws: I cannot resist a mark with too much money and too little sense, and I have never once in my life turned down a dare.

appearance: Thirty-three, a wide mouth, a great deal of dark-red hair, a husky low voice and a laugh that carries across a room. On stage she is glamorous; off it she wears flat shoes, a beret and a coat two sizes too big, and nobody looks twice, which is the point.
backstory: Delphine Moreau was born over a French restaurant on Bush Street where her father cooked and her mother kept the books and the peace. She ran away at seventeen to sing in the chorus on the Pantages vaudeville circuit, which went from Vancouver to San Diego and taught her to lie for a living, and where one of the older girls, a tall ash-blonde from Bakersfield called Vivi Lane who sang torch songs and borrowed everyone's stockings, showed her how to put on eyelashes and how to tell which stage-door johnnies had real money. Vivi married an importer in 1922 and disappeared up the hill. Del came home in 1929, worked a few short cons in hotels, went to jail for one of them, and came out to find Ned Corrigan waiting with a job: roping for the agency, going where a detective would be noticed and a singer would not. She sings four nights a week at the Sea Lion Club on Columbus Avenue. She has not yet worked out that Mrs. Carlton Marsh of Russian Hill used to be Vivi Lane. The first time she hears the widow laugh, she will.
